name: Lin Sujuan
profile: Listed on Hurun China 2007 (US$150m) via 'Rongtai Industry' in porcelain. No online source found linking a 林素娟 to a Rongtai company; the closest match is Guangdong Rongtai Industry (榕泰实业, SH:600589), a Jieyang maker of melamine 'imitation porcelain' materials, but her role there could not be verified.
notes: Identity unresolved after several Chinese-language searches. Rongtai/榕泰 link is a hypothesis only; do not use without checking Hurun 2007 list and 600589 shareholder filings on cninfo.com.cn.

name: Sadashiv Shetty
current_role: Chairman & Executive Director, Heranba Industries Ltd (Vapi, Gujarat)
profile: Sadashiv K. Shetty co-founded Heranba Industries in 1992 with Raghuram K. Shetty; it grew into a crop-protection chemicals maker and exporter (insecticides, herbicides, fungicides) based in Vapi, listed in India in 2021. He chairs the company and holds about 18% of it.
interesting_fact: Heranba's own site describes it as founded in 1992 by 'technocrats' Sadashiv K. Shetty and Raghuram K. Shetty; Sadashiv studied at the University of Mysore.
deep_cut_fact: In April 2024 he also became non-executive chairman of Daikaffil Chemicals India, a separate listed specialty-chemicals company.
notes: Wealth is shared with co-promoter Raghuram K. Shetty (Managing Director). Low media profile; corporate office in Mumbai (Borivali). Deep-cut source is an aggregator; verify with a Daikaffil BSE filing.

name: Seema Suryavanshi
current_role: Promoter/shareholder of Dilip Buildcon Ltd (Bhopal); former executive director (2006-2010)
profile: Seema Suryavanshi is a promoter of Dilip Buildcon, the Bhopal road and infrastructure EPC contractor founded by her husband Dilip Suryavanshi, who is chairman. She was a director of the company from 2006 to 2010 and has sat on boards of group entities such as Suryavanshi Infrastructure and DBL toll-road SPVs.
interesting_fact: Dilip Buildcon grew from a small Bhopal contractor into one of India's largest road builders; she was on its board when it incorporated as a company in 2006.
notes: Low public profile. Best route is through the company (head of IR Gautam Jain is named on earnings calls) or via Dilip/Rohan Suryavanshi. Her current board status is unclear: sources conflict.

name: Chen Lingyue
profile: Listed on Hurun China 2007 (US$130m) via 'Jinjia Group', printing. Most likely Shenzhen Jinjia Group (劲嘉, SZ:002191), a cigarette-pack printer that listed in 2007, but no source was found naming a 陈零越 among its founders, directors or shareholders (chairman is Qiao Luyu).
notes: Identity unresolved; the Chinese name returns no relevant hits. Check 劲嘉 2007 IPO prospectus shareholder list before any outreach.

name: Hong Zhaoshe
current_role: Chairman, Fujian Qipai Group (柒牌集团), Jinjiang
profile: Hong Zhaoshe (洪肇设, b. 1953, Yingling town, Jinjiang, Fujian) heads Qipai, a menswear brand that began as a small Jinjiang workshop in 1979 and became one of the major 'Fujian school' men's clothing groups, known for its 'Chinese stand-collar' (中华立领) suits. He is a senior engineer and was a deputy to the 10th Fujian Provincial People's Congress.
interesting_fact: Qipai's signature 中华立领 (Chinese stand-collar) line is promoted as making men's fashion distinctly Chinese; Hong wore a black Qipai stand-collar Hanfu-style suit to a 2022 brand launch.
deep_cut_fact: He was born in rural Yingling town, Jinjiang, the youngest of seven brothers, which is also where the group's early companies were registered (e.g. 晋江英林柒牌贸易).
notes: No published personal or press email found. Route via Qipai Group corporate PR in Jinjiang. Chinese-language outreach recommended.

name: Feng Yajun
profile: Listed on Hurun China 2008 (US$100m) as founder/owner of 'Zhanda Group' (展大集团) in animal feed. No online source found for 封亚军 or a feed company called 展大集团, so neither identity nor current status could be confirmed.
notes: Unresolved; possibly a small private regional feed company. Check business registries (e.g. the national enterprise credit system) with the Chinese company name.

name: Surya Prakash Madrecha
current_role: Co-founder and former Chairman & MD, Trimax IT Infrastructure & Services (Mumbai); current role unknown
profile: Udaipur-born science graduate who moved to Bombay in 1991 and co-founded Trimax IT Infrastructure & Services (incorporated 1995), growing it from a PC assembler into a systems integrator known for e-ticketing for state bus corporations (MSRTC, BEST, Rajasthan, UP, BMTC). The company entered insolvency in 2018 and was taken over by EbixCash under a 2020 resolution plan.
interesting_fact: Trimax won Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation's 2009 tender for handheld electronic ticketing machines and depot-linked software, and later built BEST's smart card (about 1.8m sold).
deep_cut_fact: 'Trimax' stands for 'try maximum'. His first job was at Sanghvi Electronics for Rs 800 a month, and his old boss Suresh Sanghvi rented him his first Lamington Road office and handed him his first two clients, Dharamsi Morarji Chemical and Arthur Andersen.
notes: Sensitive: Trimax went through insolvency (2018-2020) and lenders filed personal-guarantee proceedings against family members. Hurun wealth figure (2017-18) is likely stale. No current published contact found.

name: Janet L Cohen
current_role: Major (10%+) Symbotic shareholder through family trusts; co-trustee of The Tilia Mill Trust
profile: Janet L. Cohen is named in Symbotic's SEC filings as the wife of Symbotic founder, chairman and CEO Richard B. Cohen, and as a 10%-plus beneficial owner of the warehouse-robotics company through trusts (The Tilia Mill Trust, RBC Millennium Trust). The Cohen family fortune also comes from C&S Wholesale Grocers.
interesting_fact: Symbotic, the Wilmington, MA warehouse-automation company founded by her husband, counts Walmart as its largest customer and listed in 2022 via a SPAC merger.
notes: Private individual whose holdings are disclosed because she files as a 10% owner; SEC filings give her address only as c/o Symbotic. Better podcast target is Rick Cohen. A Feb 2024 Form 4 shows large share sales, so current stake may differ.

name: Guilherme Marques Lago
current_role: Partner, Kaszek (venture capital); Special Advisor to Nubank (CFO 2021-July 2026)
profile: Brazilian finance executive who spent about 13 years at Credit Suisse (rising to managing director), with earlier stints at McKinsey and Advent, then joined Nubank in June 2019 and became CFO in Feb 2021, steering its 2021 NYSE IPO and growth in Mexico and Colombia. He handed the CFO role to Rob Livingston in July 2026 and became a partner at Kaszek.
interesting_fact: He was CFO through Nubank's December 2021 NYSE IPO, one of the largest Latin American listings, as the company grew from a regional fintech into one of the world's largest digital banks.
deep_cut_fact: After leaving the CFO role he joined Kaszek, the VC firm that backed Nubank in its early rounds, writing that 'few companies shape Latin American technology as deeply as Kaszek'.
notes: Active on LinkedIn (announced the Kaszek move there). Kaszek is the best current route; Nubank IR is only useful for his advisory role. Kaszek role is reported by one outlet.

name: Jennifer L Sherman
current_role: President & CEO, Federal Signal Corporation (Downers Grove, IL); Chair, Franklin Electric
profile: Jennifer Sherman began as a corporate attorney, joined Federal Signal in 1994 and rose through general counsel, chief administrative officer and COO before becoming CEO on Jan 1, 2016. She has built the maker of street sweepers, vacuum trucks, safety and signalling equipment into a serial acquirer of specialty vehicle businesses. She also chairs Franklin Electric's board.
interesting_fact: She won the 2024 EY Entrepreneur Of The Year Midwest Award, unusual for a CEO of a century-old industrial company.
deep_cut_fact: Before running the company she won Outstanding Corporate Counsel awards in 2005 and 2006 from Chicago's Center for Disability and Elder Law, which helps low-income people get legal help. She also chaired the executive board of The Community House.
notes: The IR contact listed is CFO Ian Hudson. Chicago business-community figure; University of Michigan BBA and JD.

name: Henry M Nahmad
profile: Henry Nahmad, a former head of M&A at HVAC distributor Watsco (2001-2009), bought a 40% stake in EnviroStar in 2015, took control and renamed it EVI Industries in 2018. He has run a 'buy-and-build' rollup of independent commercial laundry distributors (30+ acquisitions, including Girbau North America in 2025) aiming to build North America's largest such distributor.
interesting_fact: EVI's corporate lineage goes back to Metro-Tel, a New York telephone test-equipment maker founded in 1950, which later became DRYCLEAN USA and then EnviroStar before Nahmad turned it into EVI.
deep_cut_fact: His uncle Albert Nahmad built Watsco with the same 'buy and build' playbook starting in 1972, and Henry consciously applied it to laundry equipment distribution.
notes: Low media profile; speaks mainly through earnings calls and acquisition releases. Biography source is a third-party Substack; check family/Watsco details against EVI proxy.

name: Ernest Scott Santi
current_role: Non-Executive Chairman, Illinois Tool Works; director, W.W. Grainger
profile: E. Scott Santi spent his whole career at Illinois Tool Works, rising to vice chairman (2008) and serving as CEO from 2012 through 2023. Under him ITW narrowed its portfolio and rolled out its 'ITW Business Model', lifting operating margins from about 16% to nearly 24% and more than tripling market value. He retired as an employee in March 2024 and remains non-executive chairman.
interesting_fact: He became CEO in November 2012 after the death of his predecessor David Speer, and went on to lead ITW for about 11 years.
deep_cut_fact: He began at ITW as a summer intern in 1982 and spent four decades there, eventually as CEO.
notes: Board chairs can be reached via ITW Corporate Secretary (ITWCorporateSecretary@itw.com per investor contacts page). Low-key, rarely gives interviews.

name: Mark Samuel Hoplamazian
current_role: Chairman, President & CEO, Hyatt Hotels Corporation (chairman since Feb 2026); director, VF Corp
profile: Harvard BA and Chicago Booth MBA who started in M&A at First Boston, then spent years at The Pritzker Organization, the Pritzker family's investment office, rising to president. He was made interim CEO of Hyatt in 2006, took it public in 2009 and has moved it toward an asset-light, luxury and lifestyle-heavy brand portfolio. He became board chairman in Feb 2026 when Thomas Pritzker retired.
interesting_fact: When he joined Hyatt from the Pritzker family office he recalled: 'The Pritzker Organization was 10 people. Hyatt was around 80,000', and said he 'embraced my ignorance and learned as much as I could as quickly as I could.'
deep_cut_fact: He was a Boston Consulting Group summer associate in 1988 and went to Episcopal Academy in Pennsylvania (class of 1981). His favourite advice is to say 'I don't know that yet' when facing something unfamiliar.
notes: High-profile CEO, frequent conference speaker (Skift, Milken, Aspen). Route via Hyatt corporate communications (Investor Day 2026 media contact: Franziska Weber). Avoid the Pritzker/Epstein context of his chairmanship.

name: Danny J Bartel
current_role: VP, Global Consumer Sales, Garmin Ltd (per SEC filings, 2025)
profile: Dan Bartel is a long-serving Garmin sales executive (with the company since about 1992 per one profile) who has led its worldwide and global consumer sales, covering fitness, outdoor and other consumer GPS products. His wealth comes from Garmin equity built over three decades.
interesting_fact: He has been at Garmin since 1992, three years after the company was founded in 1989, and rose to run its global consumer sales.
notes: Very low public profile; career details come from aggregator profiles (TheOrg, MarketScreener lists South Dakota State and Central Michigan universities). Not a natural podcast guest; route via Garmin corporate communications.

name: James Jeaho Rhyu
current_role: Former Chairman & CEO, Stride Inc (CEO Jan 2021-July 2026); current role not announced
profile: Penn/Wharton and London Business School graduate who began as an Ernst & Young auditor, held finance roles at XM/Sirius XM, GrafTech and Dow Jones, and was CFO/CAO of Match.com. He joined K12 in 2013 as CFO, renamed it Stride and as CEO from 2021 grew it into a $2.5bn-revenue online-education company. He left in July 2026 after 13 years.
interesting_fact: He was named CEO effective January 2021, weeks after K12 rebranded as Stride in December 2020, and led it through the pandemic surge in online schooling.
deep_cut_fact: Before education he was CFO and Chief Administrative Officer of Match.com, part of IAC.
notes: Between roles since July 2026 (succeeded by Robert Knowling); no current published contact. LinkedIn is likely the best route. Has spoken at ASU+GSV Summit.

name: Douglas E Coltharp
current_role: EVP & Chief Financial Officer, Encompass Health (since May 2010); director, Under Armour
profile: Doug Coltharp began in 1987 at NationsBank, rising to head of Southeast corporate banking, then was EVP & CFO of Saks Inc. for 11 years and a partner at Arlington Capital Advisors. He became CFO of HealthSouth (renamed Encompass Health) in 2010 and helped rebuild it into the largest US operator of inpatient rehabilitation hospitals, including the 2022 spin-off of its home health and hospice arm (Enhabit).
interesting_fact: He has been CFO of Encompass Health for over 16 years, an unusually long run for a public-company CFO, after 11 years as CFO of Saks.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career in 1987 at NationsBank (now Bank of America) and rose to senior vice president and head of Southeast Corporate Banking before moving into retail at Saks. He holds a Lehigh finance/economics degree and a Wharton MBA.
notes: Birmingham, AL based; also on the United Way of Central Alabama board (per aggregator). Speaks regularly at healthcare investor conferences. The Enhabit spin-off date is from general knowledge, not the cited bio.

name: Ram R. Krishnan
current_role: EVP & Chief Operating Officer, Emerson; director, Autodesk (and formerly AspenTech)
profile: An IIT metallurgical engineer with a Rensselaer master's and Xavier MBA, Ram Krishnan joined Emerson in 1994 as a project engineer. He ran Climate Technologies Asia from Hong Kong and integrated the $3.15bn Pentair valves acquisition as group president of Final Control. Since 2021 he has been Emerson's COO, overseeing supply chain, IT, M&A and international operations as Emerson becomes a pure-play automation company.
interesting_fact: CEO Lal Karsanbhai said Krishnan 'has turned final control into a world-class business' when promoting him to COO in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: He started at Emerson in 1994 as a project engineer and in 2011 moved to Hong Kong to run Climate Technologies in Asia, returning in 2015 in an unusually titled role: VP of 'profit planning and perfect execution'.
notes: Relevant to energy and industrial automation themes (Emerson automates power, LNG and data-center infrastructure). Also listed on USISPF's team page. AspenTech directorship ended when Emerson took AspenTech private in 2025.

name: Piyush B Sevalia
current_role: Executive Vice President, Marketing, SiTime Corp (some 2026 releases call him Chief Business Officer)
profile: Semiconductor marketer who spent about nine years at Cypress Semiconductor (from 1991), then led access-infrastructure products at Ikanos Communications before joining MEMS-timing startup SiTime in 2008. He has run marketing since 2012 and is SiTime's main voice on precision timing for AI data centers, where its oscillators help synchronise GPU clusters.
interesting_fact: He argues that poor clock synchronisation is a 'hidden tax' on AI infrastructure, with GPU utilisation in clusters as low as 20-40%, and that the industry is moving from 1-microsecond to a 10-nanosecond sync target.
deep_cut_fact: He has said the case for MEMS timing comes down to bandwidth: 'You need faster bandwidth. Because you need faster bandwidth, you need better timing.'
notes: Strong fit for a data-center podcast: experienced interviewee on AI-cluster timing. Has a SiTime newsroom author page (sitime.com/company/newsroom/author/piyush-sevalia). The podcast link is a past guest appearance, not his own show.

name: Steven Henry Gunby
current_role: Chairman, President & CEO, FTI Consulting (CEO since 2014, chairman since June 2025)
profile: Steven Gunby spent about 30 years at Boston Consulting Group, where he chaired the North and South America region (roughly tripling its revenue) and led BCG's global transformation practice. He joined FTI Consulting as CEO in 2014 and has grown the restructuring, forensic, economic and strategic-communications firm, becoming board chairman in 2025.
interesting_fact: He came to FTI from outside after three decades at BCG and turned it around. His stated philosophy: 'Changing the trajectory of a company requires major insight.'
deep_cut_fact: Before his consulting career he went to Yale Law School, where he was an editor of the law review. He also studied at Yale School of Management and Cornell.
notes: Mollie Hawkes is Head of Marketing, Communications & IR, the best corporate route. FTI has energy/power practices, which is a possible angle for an energy/data-center podcast.

name: Noel R. Wallace
current_role: Chairman, President & CEO, Colgate-Palmolive; director, American Express
profile: Texas A&M finance graduate who joined Colgate-Palmolive in 1987 and spent his career there, running the global toothbrush division, North America and Latin America before becoming president/COO in 2018. He has been CEO since April 2019 and chairman since April 2020, focusing on premium oral care, Hill's pet nutrition and sustainability.
interesting_fact: He has spent his whole career, nearly 40 years, at Colgate-Palmolive, starting in 1987.
deep_cut_fact: He ran Colgate's Global Toothbrush Division (2002-2006) and later combined the North America presidency with responsibility for global sustainability.
notes: Business Roundtable member. High-profile consumer-goods CEO; any approach goes through Colgate corporate communications. Less natural fit for an energy/data-center theme beyond sustainability.
